decisions.reason: Report locates the dangling busy in `disabled: (props.input?.phase ?? 'plain') !== 'plain' || busy`, states busy is AttachButton's useState binding and an unbound free identifier in AttachmentChips, explains the empty-occurrence early `return null` before the map, and that a present occurrence in plain phase makes the left guard false so busy is evaluated and throws ReferenceError — grounded in the fixture files.

Explains the render exception is caught by the InputZone slot error boundary which unmounts the whole dock entry (not just the remove button), that AttachButton lives in a separate input.left slot entry with its own boundary and survives, and that the diagnostic is console-only with no user-facing banner.

Uses the shipped v0.2.10 expression to establish busy already occurs in the baseline, proposes both hunk-level rollback/re-add bisection and a data-present plain-phase mount of the v0.2.10 component, does not force the claim that the hover diff is harmless (instead identifies the hoisted imageItem line as a second always-reachable defect), credits the record?.items.find TypeError, event.target.closest risks, and the diff/baseline inconsistency on the disabled line, and honestly caveats that the excerpt/full-build evidence cannot prove when historical users first exercised the failure.

Proposes deleting the bare busy (or threading explicitly owned state via props.busy), moving imageItem into the map callback where record/status are scoped, adding record?.items ?? [] / record?.items?.find hardening and event.target.closest?.()/target-type safety, while keeping the phase guard; equivalent safe fixes grounded in the fixture.

Proposes mounting the dock with at least one occurrence present, asserting the .chip exists and the error boundary captures nothing, explains why an empty-state-only test returns null before the throwing line and why node --check only parses and cannot resolve free identifiers or execute the component, and requires this data-present smoke in pre-ship checks.
